author: Taylor Mitchell
title: Huntsville employee fired after pleading guilty to $73 thousand theft - NewsBreak
text:
By Taylor Mitchell Logan Sparkman ,
6 hours ago
HUNTSVILLE, Ala. (WHNT) — The city of Huntsville says a woman who pleaded guilty to stealing from a local youth sports league has been fired from her job with the city.
The city told News 19 Thursday that it has fired Heather Spier job with the city's landscape management department.
Nine arrested in HPD operation targeting gun violence "Heather Spier’s employment with the City of Huntsville was terminated, effective Oct. 21, 2026, in accordance with the City’s Personnel Policies and Procedures," a city spokesperson said. "The City will have no further comment."
Spier pleaded guilty to first-degree theft charges on Sept. 29. Court documents show Heather Ann Spier stole $73,225 from the Huntsville Eastern League from September 2022 to February 2024.
As part of her plea, Spier received a 46-month sentence, but it is suspended, so she won’t have to spend any time behind bars unless she violates her probation over the next two years.
She was also ordered to pay the Eastern League the full amount that she admitted to taking within seven days of the sentencing.
The Eastern League is “the recreational youth sports league serving families in the Hampton Cove, Owens Cross Roads, and Monte Sano areas of Huntsville, Alabama,” according to its website.
